---
title: "Outcome Measures"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
Outcome measure selection is provisional pending literature review completion.
Measures marked **[CONFIRM]** need validation from existing studies.
:::

## Primary Outcome: Centre of Pressure Timing

**What**: The frame at which COP transitions from predominantly trail foot to
predominantly lead foot, relative to top of backswing.

**Why**: This is the specific mechanism the device is designed to train —
earlier, more consistent trail-to-lead COP shift at transition. Literature
consistently identifies this as distinguishing skilled from less skilled golfers.

**How measured**:
- Gold standard: Force plates (Swing Catalyst / Kistler) — 1000Hz, direct measurement
- Feasible option: Pressure insoles (Moticon ~100Hz) — validated against force plates
  for gross COP measures **[CONFIRM validation in golf context]**
- Minimum viable: Face-on video — manual frame coding, indirect proxy

**Key reference**: GRF systematic review (Sports Medicine 2026) for what
constitutes a meaningful difference.

---

## Primary Outcome: COP Magnitude

**What**: Peak force under trail foot during backswing; peak force under lead
foot at and after impact; expressed as % body weight.

**Why**: Literature (BodiTrak data, Hashimoto) shows skilled golfers produce
>100% body weight under lead foot at transition. This is trainable.

**How measured**: Same as COP timing above.

---

## Secondary Outcome: Ball Direction Consistency

**What**: Standard deviation of launch direction across 10 shots per session.

**Why**: If COP change is meaningful it should eventually manifest in ball
outcome. Direction is more sensitive than distance for detecting swing path
changes.

**How measured**: Launch monitor (TrackMan, GC3, or Mevo) if accessible at
the instructor's facility.

**[TO RESOLVE]**: Does the instructor have access to a launch monitor?

---

## Secondary Outcome: Subjective Feel Rating

**What**: Participant rates "how in control did that feel" 1-10 after each
session block.

**Why**: Proprioceptive interventions should produce changes in subjective
body awareness before they appear in objective measures. Also captures
compliance and engagement.

**How measured**: Simple paper form per session.

---

## Natural Variability Baseline

**Critical consideration**: Before interpreting any change, we need to know
the natural swing-to-swing variability for each participant.

The GRF systematic review (Sports Medicine 2026) specifically notes reliability
of GRF data is "substantially less clear" than the measures themselves —
what represents a true change vs natural bandwidth is unestablished.

**Proposed**: Collect 10+ swings at T0 to establish within-participant
variability before attributing any T1/T2 change to the intervention.

---

## Measures NOT included and why

**Clubhead speed**: Too many confounders (effort level, fatigue). Not
sensitive to weight transfer specifically.

**Handicap / score**: Changes over weeks are too slow and too confounded
by course conditions, weather, mental state.

**X-factor**: Camera-angle dependent as discussed in literature review.
Not reliable from single-camera setup.

**3D kinematics**: Requires motion capture lab — out of scope for
preliminary study.
